disease_label_per_paper: Massive pulmonary embolism diagnosed by bedside ultrasound with lower-extremity DVT and right-heart strain
presentation_summary: 61-year-old ill-appearing man presented to the emergency department with one week of dyspnea, generalized weakness, and near syncope.
EMS found unstable vital signs and an indeterminate supraventricular tachycardia; two rounds of adenosine did not improve the rhythm.
On arrival systolic blood pressure was 70 mmHg, heart rate 140-160/min, respiratory rate 22/min, and SpO2 88-90% on a 10 L non-rebreather mask.
Focused history revealed left calf charley-horse pain for several days before presentation.
Bedside ultrasound showed extensive thromboses in the left femoral and popliteal veins, right-heart strain, a mobile 2.84 cm right atrial thrombus, enlarged RV, hyperdynamic LV, and McConnell sign.
The patient was treated with IV tissue plasminogen activator, then warfarin and an inferior vena cava filter, and survived to discharge.

quality_warnings: This case is a post-bedside-ultrasound PE test: no CTPA was available before treatment, but duplex DVT plus echo RV strain/right-heart thrombus are rankable evidence-stage observations.
The paper diagnosis and response to tPA are preserved as non-ranking evidence.
